1 1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 LAC no. 215/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))
Balbir Singh & Ors. V. Union of India Page no. 2 of 12 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".

entities.text: Balbir Singh & Ors. V. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 U/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 Bighas 01 Biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are recorded owner/ cobhumidar of the land bearing Khasra no.
11//18/2 (204), 23/1 (400) total measuring 06 Bighas and 04 Biswas situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.
It is stated that the petitioners are the bhumidhar/absolute owner and in cultivatory possession of the said land till the notice under Section 4 LAC no. 215/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))
Balbir Singh & Ors. V. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 of the Act was issued.

entities.text: Balbir Singh & Ors. V. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said land is free from all encumbrances and no litigation in respect of the said land is pending before any court of law.

6. It is stated that the said notification and the impugned award are illegal, bad in law and violative of all principles of natural justice and provisions of law, highly insufficient interalia on the following grounds:
(i) The learned LAC has assessed the compensation merely on the basis of surmises and conjectures and without looking into the actual market rate of land prevailing in the area.
The LAC has not considered the factum of intrinsic value which in here in the said land, and the location of the land while assessing its market value.

The said land is surrounded by Industrial Area of Bawana (recently developed by DSIDC),
Residential Area of Rohini and several Godowns, Farm Houses, private colonies of villages and factories where the government have provided all civic amentities like roads, bus services, drainage, railway facilities, electricity, school, colleges, hospitals Balbir Singh Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51869079/
2 and telecommunication, etc.
The land of the petitioner is quite leveled one and is fit for residential/ commercial, industry and buildings without making any level thereof.
(ii) The respondent no. 1 has fixed the market price of the land without considering the actual prevailing market price of the land.
The land of the petitioners could not be tagged at any amount less than Rs. 5,000/ per sq. yards.
Earlier, DSIDC had provided the adjoining land to the Industrial Units @more than Rupees 10,000 per sq. yard and DDA has LAC no. 215/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Balbir Singh & Ors.
V. Union of India Page no. 4 of 12 been allotting the acquired land at a minimum rate of about Rs. 8,000/ per sq. yards.
(iii) The learned LAC has also erred in not including the land of the petitioners which is very fertile and productive and gives at least three crops in a year.
The land is having a watercourse connected with the Canal.
The petitioners and his family members are dependant on the agricultural income and are now left with insufficient source of income.
The entire agricultural equipments and paraphernalia such as tractor, cultivator, harrow trolley, etc costing about Rs. 4 lakhs has become complete waste.
(iv) The land still in possession of the petitioners is well fertile and productive and their existed vegetable crops all the time of demarcation of land done by respondent no. 1.

The learned LAC has also made error in not taking into account the devaluation of money if the date and year of the above said notification is taken to be the base, date and year, then the LAC was bound to determine the compensation by taking into consideration the market value of the land on the date of publication of the notification on the basis of loss and injury suffered by the petitioner.
Therefore, the compensation awarded by the LAC is only 50% of the market value.

(v) The learned LAC has also erred in not awarding the compensation for the expenses, loss and injury sustained by the petitioner LAC no. 215/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Balbir Singh & Ors. V. Union of India Page no. 5 of 12 due to competed change of nature and place of business/ livelihood.

entities.text: Balbir Singh & Ors. V. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The LAC has also grossly erred in not considering the yearly increasy of 12% in the value of the land between 01.04.2001 to 21.03.2003.

(vi) The petitioners was having a tube well run by electric/diesel engine and in the said land, which was in good condition and working effectively when the award of the land was announced by the LAC and has grossly erred in not awarding adequate compensation for boaring of the tubewells and equipments such as pipe, Etc.
(x) It is prayed that the petitioners by way of present petition are claiming market value of the said land @ Rs. 5,000 per square yards.

The petitioners also claim Rs. 80,000/ per Bigha for loss and damages sustained by the petitioners by reason of damages sustained by him on account of having deprived of farming on the land for crops and vegetables.

The petitioners further claim a sum of Rs.
4 lakhs on account of boaring of tubewells and cost of equipment such as pipe, etc and one well and Balbir Singh Ors.

3 construction of pucca room.

The petitioners claims Rs. 4 lakhs for the damages sustained by the petitioners for acquisition of the land compulsory and injuriously affecting his other properties such as his residential house and agriculture equipments such as tractor, cultivator, etc.
The petitioner further claim a sum of Rs. 5 lakhs in consequence of the acquisition of the land as the petitioners have to change his place of business.

The petitioner further claims the interest at the rate of 18 %
p.a. without any tax LAC no. 215/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Balbir Singh & Ors. V.
Union of India Page no. 6 of 12 deductions and he may also be awarded the just and legal solatium as per law.

sentences.text: The respondent is directed to provide the alternate plots to the petitioner as per rules.

7. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 / Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) and, it is, inter alia, submitted that the notification under Section 4 was passed on 21.03.2003 and the declaration under Section 6 of the Act was issued on 19.03.2004 and the said land has been acquired for the public purposes i.e. for Planned Development of Delhi.

It is submitted that the learned LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view all the aspects and has assessed the market value after considering the level of development,
locality and situation of the area where the said land is situated.

The Ld. LAC has assessed the fair market value of the said land by adopting the indicative price fixed by the government of NCT of Delhi @ Rs. 15,70,000 per acre for the year 2001 - 2002, which is applicable with effect from 01.04.2001.
The Ld. LAC adopted the indicative price fixed by the Government of NCT of Delhi of land falling in "Block A".

As far as the land having ghadda upto 23 feet, the ld. LAC has deducted Rs. 1,70,000 per acre from the market value of "Block B" category land, therefore, after deduction the value comes to Rs. 14,00,000 per acre, and as such the market value of the said land was assessed as per the rate prevailing during the corresponding period for different categories of land besides other statutory benefits.
The market value of the land falling in the "Block C" consisting of gaddhas upto LAC no. 215/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Balbir Singh & Ors.
V. Union of India Page no. 7 of 12 46 feet was assessed at Rs. 12,30,000/ per acre as the earth has been taken out for making bricks, etc.

8. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village Mubarakpur Dabas had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to Ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

9. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.

The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect LAC no.
Balbir Singh Ors.

4 215/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Balbir Singh & Ors. V. Union of India Page no. 8 of 12 to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.
10.

sentences.text: It is submitted that the said land, after acquisition, the possession of the land has been taken over by DDA on 04.04.2006 and subsequently handed over to RPD VII.

It is submitted that the compensation passed by ld. LAC is legal, adequate, just and fair and the same has been awarded by ld. LAC after taking into consideration all the factors relevant for determining the compensation, as such the petitioner is not entitled for grant of enhancement of compensation.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition are denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action,
therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed with cost.

11. On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 12.08.2014:  ISSUES:
1.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent?

OPP.
2. Relief.
12.
Matter was, thereafter, listed for recording of petitioners evidence.
LAC no. 215/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Balbir Singh & Ors.
V. Union of India Page no. 9 of 12 13.

Ld. Counsel for the petitioners as well as Ld. Counsels for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 195 of 2016, Savitri Devi Vs. Union of India.

entities.text: Savitri Devi Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
14. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for DDA.
None had appeared on behalf of petitioner and UOI to address the final arguments.
Petitioner and UOI have even failed to file written submissions, though opportunity was granted.
Therefore, this Court deems it fit to pass judgment on merits of the case.

My issuewise findings and determination are as under: 
1. Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent?
OPP.
15.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
16. To prove their case, the petitioners, through his counsel has adopted the evidence led in case Savitri Devi (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 05.09.2023 and Ld.

Counsel for the petitioners have argued that the Balbir Singh Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51869079/
5

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioner in the aforementioned case.
LAC no. 215/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Balbir Singh & Ors. V. Union of India Page no. 10 of 12 17.

entities.text: Balbir Singh & Ors. V. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

18. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value as awarded in the case of Savitri Devi (supra) in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

19. In the case of Savitri Devi (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 as Rs. 19,45,800/
per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Savitri Devi (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
20 . The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the LAC no. 215/ 2016 (Award No. 16/2005 06/DC(NW)) Balbir Singh & Ors. V. Union of India Page no. 11 of 12 petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.

entities.text: Balbir Singh & Ors. V. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 21.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2)
Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).

(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
22.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
